title: Weather
goal: Say what the weather is like, and understand a forecast.

vocabulary.example: The sun is very strong today.
Take a coat, it's going to rain.
There isn't a cloud in the sky.
The wind is cold this morning.
There was a storm last night.
The fog is thick near the river.
A warm evening is perfect for the beach.
It is dry from June to December.
The forecast says rain on Sunday.

phrases.use: The normal question. Not how is the weather.
Happening now. Use the -ing form for weather in progress.
You can see it coming — dark clouds, wind.
Small talk. The tag falls, it is not a real question.

phrases.text: Take an umbrella, just in case.
phrases.use: Advising someone before they go out.

lines.text: What's the weather like out there?
Grey. It's going to rain, I think.
Really? It was thirty degrees yesterday.
I know. The forecast says storms all week.
Take an umbrella too, just in case.

questions.q: What does B think will happen?

reading.title: Two seasons, not four
reading.text:
Textbooks teach four seasons, and for most of Brazil that is simply wrong. In Recife there is a wet season and a dry season, and everybody plans around which one they are in rather than around spring or autumn. This causes a small problem in English lessons, because the language has a whole set of words built for a climate the learner has never lived in: frost, sleet, drizzle, mild. A student can define them perfectly and still have no feeling for what they mean.

The practical answer is not to skip them but to learn them the way you learn the vocabulary of a film: as something real people use somewhere else. You will need them the first time you read a forecast abroad, or the first time an English person opens a conversation with the weather, which they will, within about a minute of meeting you.

questions.q: What does the writer say about the four seasons?
options: They do not describe most of Brazil

questions.q: Why are words like drizzle hard?
options: The learner has not lived in that climate
Learn them as vocabulary used elsewhere

It is very hot and there is no rain. The season is ___.
